study_identification.title: Fractionating autism based on neuroanatomical normative modeling

study_characteristics.study_objective: To introduce a novel methodological framework for parsing neuroanatomical subtypes within a large cohort of individuals with autism.

quality_checking_detail.answer: Visual assessment of surface reconstructions by at least 3 independent raters. Exclusion of scans with severe artifacts. Freesurfer Euler number used as a proxy for scan quality.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Gaussian process regression with dummy coded site variables.

predictor_variables.answer: Age; Sex; Full-scale IQ; Site; Freesurfer Euler number

predictor_effects.answer: Site was modeled as a dummy coded variable.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The normative model included site as a covariate, addressing potential site effects.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Brie /uniFB02 y, for each participant, we estimated normative models to predict vertex-wise cortical thickness as a function of age and sex plus nuisance covariates including full-scale IQ, plus dummy coded site variables and the Freesurfer Euler number (a proxy for scan quality) using Gaussian process regression.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The model was validated using 10-fold cross-validation on the training dataset.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: We used 10-fold cross-validation during the training process to provide an unbiased estimation of the model.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study did not use an independent dataset from the same domain for validation.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study did not use a dataset from a different domain for validation.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Spearman's correlation between the atypicality index with ADOS-2 and ADI-R scores, Social Responsiveness Scale-2 (SRS-2), Repetitive Behavioral Scale-Revised (RBS-R) and Short Sensory Pro /uniFB01 le (SSP), along with the DSM-5 parent-rated scale for attention de /uniFB01 cit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms (inattention and hyper-impulsivity), both across the whole cohort and within each cluster.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study identified five putative neuroanatomical subtypes of autism, which showed distinct patterns of cortical thickness alterations and were associated with different clinical and genetic features.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Five biologically based putative subtypes were derived using normative modeling of CT and spectral clustering. Three of these clusters showed relatively widespread decreased CT and two showed relatively increased CT. These subtypes showed morphometric differences from one another, providing a potential explanation for inconsistent case-control findings in autism, and loaded differentially and more strongly onto symptoms and polygenic risk, indicating a dilution of clinical effects across heterogeneous cohorts.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Large number of missing clinical and behavioral data, which complicated analyses and led to a reduction of power in follow-up analyses. No manual edits on the cortical surface reconstructions.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study used spectral clustering on the individual-level deviations from a normative model of CT development to identify subtypes.
